title: Reverse refuted predicate-lock tightening: restore coarsest SIRead granularity
configuration_cause: Incumbent runs max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0 (coarsest SIRead granularity). Experiment 012 reversed these to defaults (2, -2) and was reject_harmful: TPS fell 8-10% and locks_total.p95 rose from ~330 to ~2146/2013, with GetUserTweets p99 rising 493->1219/1149us. The default-granularity direction is falsified; the incumbent's coarse setting is the better regime.
mechanism: Experiment 012 tested moving predicate-lock granularity from the incumbent extreme (0,0) toward PostgreSQL defaults (2,-2) and was reject_harmful: locks_total.p95 exploded ~6x and GetUserTweets p99 roughly doubled, cutting TPS ~9%. Per the paired-decision policy, reject_harmful falsifies the tested direction, so we reverse it with equal-or-larger safe amplitude: push both caps to their safe low bound 0 (already incumbent) is not a change, so instead we test the remaining untested axis of the same SIRead family — the per-transaction budget max_pred_locks_per_transaction — raising it 8192->16384 to give each SERIALIZABLE transaction a larger SIRead budget, delaying promotion to coarser granularity and reducing promotion churn without re-tightening the page/relation caps that 012 showed are load-bearing.
query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.876); a larger per-txn SIRead budget should reduce predicate-lock promotion churn on its index scans, trimming p99 without adding lock waits (lock_waiting_backends.max is 0).
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (>=0.3%) if promotion churn is budget-bound; unchanged if the incumbent's coarse page/relation caps already absorb promotion.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 flat-to-slightly-down; no regression expected since lock_waiting_backends.max is 0.

predictions.rationale: Larger per-txn SIRead budget delays promotion, reducing lock bookkeeping churn versus incumbent 8192.
Less promotion churn on the dominant transaction trims its tail.
Freed terminal capacity from GetUserTweets raises completed-transaction goodput.
No lock waits observed at incumbent; larger budget should not introduce waits.

alternatives.statement: If promotion churn is already absorbed by the incumbent's coarse page/relation caps, raising max_pred_locks_per_transaction yields no measurable change in locks_total.p95 or TPS.
If the residual bottleneck is WAL commit-path queueing rather than predicate locks, TPS stays flat and wal_waiting_backends.p95 remains >=1 regardless of SIRead budget.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent already sits at the coarsest page/relation caps that 012 proved load-bearing; the untested per-transaction SIRead budget is the remaining lever in the same family and can only reduce promotion churn, not re-tighten the caps that 012 showed harmful.

nodes.label: Larger per-txn SIRead budget delays promotion, reducing predicate-lock churn

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Double from incumbent 8192 to the safe high bound 16384 (allowed [64,16384]); 2x per-txn SIRead budget to test whether promotion churn is budget-bound, distinct from the refuted 012 page/relation-cap direction.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: per-transaction SIRead lock budget governing promotion to coarser granularity

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage owns the WAL commit-path bundle; wal_waiting_backends.p95=1 persists and may cap gains from this SIRead action
